issues.legal_issue: A Hindu widow cannot validly surrender her entire estate jointly to the next heir and a person who is not the next heir.
material_facts: After the widow's death, the mother-in-law was said to have relinquished the estate in favour of two relatives in equal shares.
Only one of the two relatives was the next heir under Hindu law; the other was not.
The reversioners later claimed the estate after the mother-in-law's death.
issues.conclusion: The purported surrender was invalid because it was not made exclusively in favour of the next heir, and succession opened when the mother-in-law died.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu law, the doctrine of surrender operates by vesting the estate in the next heir and cannot be used to vest any part of it in a stranger. A surrender to the next heir together with another person is invalid. The Court followed Mummareddi Nagireddi v. Pitti Durairaja Naidu [1951] S.C.R. 655.

predicates.reversionary_estate_claim: A person claiming as a reversioner seeks the deceased husband's estate after the limited holder's death.
predicates.widow_purported_to_surrender_estate: A Hindu widow purported to relinquish her interest in the estate.
predicates.surrender_included_non_next_heir: The purported surrender directed some of the estate to a person who was not the next heir.

issues.definition: When a reversioner claims the estate after a widow purported to surrender it to a group that included someone other than the next heir, the surrender is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A compromise made by a widow does not bind reversioners when it protects her interests but is not a prudent and reasonable settlement for the estate or the reversioners.
material_facts: A widow, acting for herself and as guardian of a minor widow, compromised a suit brought by relatives claiming the estate under an alleged will.
The compromise preserved the widows' rights under Hindu law and provided that the claimants would take the estate after the widows' deaths, although they were not then the heirs under Hindu law.
The widows gave up none of their own rights, and the interests of the ultimate reversioners were neither considered nor protected.
The compromise was found to have been made for the personal benefit of the widows rather than as a prudent settlement for the estate.
issues.conclusion: The compromise was not a bona fide, prudent, or reasonable settlement for the estate and did not bind the reversioners.
issues.legal_principle: A decree fairly and properly obtained against a female heir concerning the estate can bind reversioners, and a bona fide compromise in the course of a suit can have the same effect when made for the estate's benefit rather than the limited owner's personal advantage. Whether the compromise is bona fide depends on its substance; it must be prudent and reasonable in the circumstances. The Court relied on Venayeck Anundrow v. Luxumeebaee (1861–1863) 9 M.I.A. 520, Ramsumaran Prasad v. Shyam Kumari (1922) 49 I.A. 342, Mohendra Nath Biswas v. Shamsunnessa Khatun (1915) 21 C.L.J. 157, and Imrit Kunwar v. Roop Narain Singh (1880) 6 C.L.R. 76. It distinguished Mata Prasad v. Nageshar Sahai (1925) 52 I.A. 393.

rule.if: reversionary_estate_dispute and widow_compromised_suit_concerning_estate and compromise_preserved_widows_rights and compromise_ignored_reversioners

predicates.reversionary_estate_dispute: A dispute concerns whether reversioners are entitled to an estate after a female holder's death.
predicates.widow_compromised_suit_concerning_estate: A widow representing herself or a minor female holder entered into a compromise in a suit concerning the estate.
predicates.compromise_preserved_widows_rights: The compromise preserved the widows' rights without requiring them to give up any of their own interests.
predicates.compromise_ignored_reversioners: The compromise did not consider or safeguard the interests of the ultimate reversioners.

issues.definition: In a dispute over an estate claimed by reversioners, a compromise that preserves the widows' rights while ignoring the reversioners' interests does not bind the reversioners.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee relying on an ostensible ownership derived from a limited estate cannot use the protection for transfers by ostensible owners against reversioners after that limited estate ends.
material_facts: A transferee bought property from persons claiming ownership through an arrangement involving a female holder who had only a limited life estate.
The transferee invoked the protection for transfers by an ostensible owner against the reversioner's claim.
The reversioner sought the estate after the limited holder's death.
issues.conclusion: The transferee could not rely on section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act against the reversioner; that protection was available only during the limited owner's lifetime.
issues.legal_principle: Section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act does not protect a transferee against a reversioner's claim when the ostensible ownership derives from a limited estate; its operation is confined to the lifetime of the limited owner.

predicates.reversioner_claims_against_transferee: A reversioner seeks property from a transferee after the limited holder's death.
predicates.transferor_claimed_through_ostensible_ow: The transferor claimed to hold the position of ostensible owner when transferring the property.
predicates.ostensible_title_derived_from_limited_es: The asserted ostensible ownership arose from an arrangement involving a holder with only a limited estate.
predicates.limited_holder_has_died: The holder of the limited estate had died before the reversioner's claim was decided.

issues.definition: A transferee cannot resist a reversioner's claim on the basis of ostensible ownership derived from a limited estate after the limited holder has died.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to a plaintiff's standing based on an alleged relinquishment cannot be raised for the first time at a late appellate stage when it was not disputed or preserved earlier.
material_facts: The defendants raised the contention that the plaintiff had relinquished her rights in favour of her sons and therefore lacked standing.
The plaint had alleged that the relinquishment was inoperative and void.
The defendants did not dispute that allegation in the earlier proceedings and did not raise the contention at the proper stages or in their grounds of appeal.
issues.conclusion: The defendants could not raise the standing contention at that stage, and the contention was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: A party cannot raise at a late appellate stage a contention that could have been raised earlier but was not; where the opposing party's pleading stated that the relinquishment was inoperative and the allegation was not disputed, the opposing party may also have been deprived of the opportunity to prove that it had ceased to operate or to amend the pleading.

rule.if: estate_recovery_appeal and standing_challenge_based_on_relinquishment and relinquishment_invalidity_pleaded and challenge_not_preserved_earlier

predicates.estate_recovery_appeal: An appeal arises from a suit seeking recovery of an estate.
predicates.standing_challenge_based_on_relinquishme: A party argues that the plaintiff lacks standing because she relinquished her rights to others.
predicates.relinquishment_invalidity_pleaded: The plaintiff pleaded that the alleged relinquishment was inoperative or void.
predicates.challenge_not_preserved_earlier: The opposing party did not dispute that pleading or raise the standing challenge at the proper earlier stages.

issues.definition: In an appeal from an estate-recovery suit, a standing challenge based on relinquishment is rejected when the plaintiff pleaded that the relinquishment was inoperative and the opposing party did not preserve the challenge earlier.
